audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: the matchup never names a single Yone ability. The pages say 'W-cleave', 'E spirit-rewind', 'Q dash', 'his R' throughout.
audit.why: Riot's real names are Mortal Steel (Q), Spirit Cleave (W), Soul Unbound (E) and Fate Sealed (R). Descriptive nicknames make the advice unsearchable and unverifiable for the reader.
audit.corrected: Used the real names in every line I rewrote, and added the two facts that matter: Soul Unbound leaves his body behind (22s at rank 1, 10s at rank 5) and Spirit Cleave is 14s with a shield that scales with champions hit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 3 was scored as Yone and level 6 as Karma, and diff read EVEN while diffRating said 8/10 and the summary said 'Hard matchup'.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Karma, Skill, Skill, Yone, Yone, Yone, Yone. The content why for level 3 literally says 'still a coin flip' — that is a Skill row, not a Yone row — and the level 6 why describes Fate Sealed beating Karma's re-empowerment, so it cannot be hers.
audit.corrected: Row 2 to Skill and row 4 to Yone on both layers; diff set to HARD to match the rating already on the page.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phase whys were champion boilerplate ('the lane is a toll booth and you own it') that named no Yone spike.
audit.why: His curve is Soul Unbound coming online around 4 (the lane flips), Fate Sealed at 6 (120s at rank 1, pulls and knocks up), and his first crit item. Karma has no level-6 spike.
audit.corrected: Rewrote phases[0..6].why against those spikes using the real ability names.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns called Soul Unbound 'his burst window' with no duration or cooldown.
audit.why: 22/19/16/13/10s. At rank 1 that is a genuine 22-second punish window; by rank 5 it is 10 and the pattern stops working — a distinction the page never drew.
audit.corrected: Both endpoints stated, plus the pre-cast rule for Fate Sealed (Inspire is a shield and never stops a knockup).

edits.before: Q poke at level 1 is among the best in the game — chunk Yone on every last-hit and start the Mantra economy.
edits.after: You own level 1 — RQ Soulflare's zone and slow land before Soul Unbound exists to walk him out of it.

edits.before: W tether threatens the root — anyone who steps to you early eats Q-W and donates the trade.
edits.after: It evens fast — Mortal Steel trades back, so your Inner Flame stops pulling clean value.

edits.before: Full kit: E shield-speed makes you untouchable in short trades. Mantra-Q (RQ) on cooldown gaps is a third of his HP.
edits.after: Coin flip: you can poke, but Spirit Cleave punishes any step-up and his E is one level from blanking your rhythm.

edits.before: Spam the RQ slow-field on his farming spots and keep your shield for Soul Unbound — the lane is a toll booth and you own it.
edits.after: Soul Unbound dives your poke, Spirit Cleave lands, and he rewinds before your W root resolves — your cooldown game falls apart.

edits.before: No new ultimate at 6 — your Mantra has been online since level 1. His spike is the danger window: respect it.
edits.after: Fate Sealed pulls you in and knocks you up — Inspire is a shield, so it soaks the burst but never stops the airborne.

edits.before: First item amplifies the RQ chunk — keep him under 60% and the lane stays yours by default.
edits.after: His first crit item sharpens the cleave-and-rewind all-in; your AP item sharpens dodgeable poke.

edits.before: You drift toward utility now — peel, shield, and speed your carries while the RQ poke softens objectives.
edits.after: He out-duels your thin frame with crit and two-form mobility — no late spike answers it, so play safe.

edits.before: His dash beats your poke rhythm — shield the engage, root the exit, and respect the all-in windows.
edits.after: Soul Unbound rewinds him out of your root — win the first three levels, then pre-shield and kite.

edits.before: His dash beats your poke rhythm — shield the engage, root the exit, and respect the all-in windows.
edits.after: Soul Unbound rewinds him out of your root — win the first three levels, then pre-shield and kite.

edits.before: Tax the approach, survive the dive, and grind him down between windows. Soul Unbound is the clock this lane runs on — read it before every step forward.
edits.after: Bank levels 1-3, then stop stepping up. Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1 — his body stays behind while the spirit is out, and that is where he has to return.

edits.before: - Yone Soul Unbound: matchup-defining — His burst window — survive it and punish the body he snaps back to. It governs your forward steps. - E shield spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Soul Unbound: 22s at rank 1, 10s at rank 5 — while the spirit is out his body waits behind, and that is where he snaps back to. - Spirit Cleave is 14s and shields more per champion hit. - Pre-cast E for Fate Sealed; it never stops the knockup.

edits.before: Track Yone’s Soul Unbound: His burst window — survive it and punish the body he snaps back to. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1 and 10s at rank 5 — his body waits behind while the spirit dives, and he must return to it.

edits.before: Open the toll booth: Q every last-hit, RQ the cooldown gaps, and hold E strictly for Soul Unbound. The lane is yours until he spikes.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are the window: RQ Soulflare his step-ups before Soul Unbound exists, and hold E for Fate Sealed, never for poke.

notes: I kept the wording about Yone's body to what Riot's own text supports ('Yone's spirit leaves his body behind... forced back to his body'). Whether the abandoned body can be rooted or attacked is NOT in the kit text and I did not assert it — the existing full-layer line 'punish the body he snaps back to' already implied more than the data proves, so I softened it to 'that is where he snaps back to'. If someone can confirm the body's targetability, that would make this matchup's advice much sharper.
